We're starting to plan a quarterly maintenance window for our Redwood Private deployment (VPC) and want to confirm best practices around version pinning and staged upgrades. Two quick asks: 1) can Redwood provide a recommended pinning strategy so we don't accidentally float into a new model/runtime without a canary? 2) do you have a playbook for a 3-stage rollout (canary, cohort, full) including rollback triggers?

I've attached our current patch inventory (quanta_patch_inventory.xlsx) which lists our current OpenModel build, runtime, and kube versions. We're targetting the week of May 24 for the first maintenance window but flexible.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call.

Ravi — thanks for the inventory; got it. High level answers up front: pin the service package (runtime + model artifact) per-cluster, use a canary pool (1–2 nodes) with synthetic traffic & smoke tests, then expand by cohort. Rollback policy should be automatic if error rate or tail latency crosses threshold for >2 consecutive evaluation windows.

I'll attach our compact compatibility matrix and a condensed rollout checklist. Quick proposed cadence:
- Day 0 (pre-check): backup KV caches, snapshot configs, record pinned hashes
- Day 1 (canary): deploy to canary pool + 60m smoke tests
- Day 2 (cohort): expand to 25% nodes, monitor 6 hours
- Day 3 (full): expand remainder, monitor 24 hours

Key triggers to abort/rollback: 5% increase in 99th pct latency, 3x increase in error rate, or degradation in eval prompt set score > 2 points.

I'll draft a mutual action plan and include rollback runbook items. Would you prefer weekends or a weekday evening window?

Attachments: redwood_private_compat_matrix.pdf

Ravi / Mina — adding technical constraints from the runtime side. A couple of specifics that affect your plan:

1) Version pinning: we recommend a triple-pin — model artifact sha, runtime package (redwood-runtime x.y.z), and quantized weights profile. We can serve a different model artifact under the same API route if you explicitely opt-in, but automatic float is disabled by default on Private.

2) Canary sizing: for low-traffic Quanta clusters we suggest 2 GPUs (or equivalent vCPU config) with synthetic traffic that mirrors your 95th percentile request size. If you run our KV prefix caching heavily, bring canary traffic up to emulate warm cache hit ratios.

3) Rollback hooks: we publish a /health/upgrade endpoint that returns a JSON summary (memory, kv-hit, latency distribution, model perplexity on checks). Our orchestrator can perform automatic rollback when the endpoint indicates non-recovery.

Operational notes: make sure NAT gateway flows and private peering routes are captured in the pre-check (we've seen packet MTU issues during kube image pulls across some cloud peering). Also, store your snapshots in an external S3-compatible bucket reachable from the private control plane — don't rely solely on local PVs for rollback snapshots.

Ravi / team — flagged a couple of compliance & evidence items you'll want to capture during the window for your auditors (SOC 2 / HIPAA posture):
- Audit log export of upgrade actions (timestamps, operator, artifact hashes) — keep a copy externally
- Configuration drift snapshot (pre and post) stored in immutable storage
- Retention note: if you run rollbacks, keep both artifact sets and the audit trail for 180 days

If Quanta wants us to sign off on the rollback decision (so it becomes a joint approval), we'll need an on-call contact list and an escalation path documented in the mutual action plan.
